findings: Vertex capacity alone preserves historical pixels and coverage, but is about 3.8% slower than the average bracketing baseline and uses more process memory on the captured workload. It was not installed alone.

Triangle compiled graphs accept viewport dimensions as runtime inputs. The combined candidate reuses independent complete pipelines across target sizes and buckets vertex capacity, with a 24-entry retention policy.

Across 32 target sizes repeated twice, candidate takes 8869 ms; bracketing baselines take 24621 and 24882 ms. Sampled peak private memory is 40.9 MB versus 276.3 and 268.0 MB. This is a controlled packet workload, not desktop throughput.

Across 32 texture layouts repeated twice, candidate takes 40524 ms; baselines take 50029 then 20692 ms. Disk-cache warmup changes the baseline substantially. The candidate is 96% slower than the warm baseline as its smaller cache evicts pipelines. No general speedup is established.
All 384 synthetic packets pass independent full-pixel and coverage expectations. All 71 historical candidate outputs preserve exact pixels, coverage, device and protocol flags.

Initial v2 build fails because an explicit cmath include is missing. v2b corrects that include. Initial synthetic packets use invalid sequence 4101, exceeding protocol maximum 4096; v3 changes only sequence assignment to 3501 through 3564. Both failures and baseline recovery are preserved.
The 24-entry policy tests a resource-retention hypothesis after v113 queue creation failures; no hardware queue limit or prevention of desktop device loss is established.
